summary: Surveys use cases and operational experience with Multipath TCP in real networks, including heuristics that helped and ideas for improvement. It is informational.

eli5.summary: Multipath TCP lets one download use several roads at once. This is a report on where people actually used it and what they learned.

subtitle: Real-world deployment lessons from using TCP over multiple paths

tldr.problem: Multipath TCP (MPTCP) was specified as experimental, but real-world deployment revealed operational challenges that needed to be documented and addressed.
tldr.mechanism: This informational RFC surveys actual use cases, deployment experiences, and practical heuristics learned from running MPTCP in live networks, covering datacenters, mobile devices, and proxy scenarios.
tldr.outcome: The document guides implementers and operators on handling middlebox interference, congestion control strategies, subflow management, and networking edge cases that affect MPTCP performance.

today: RFC 8041 is an Informational RFC documenting real-world MPTCP experience from 2017. Multipath TCP is defined in RFC 6824 as Experimental and has not been updated or obsoleted. MPTCP deployment continues to grow, particularly on mobile devices. The operational lessons documented here guide implementers and operators on making MPTCP work reliably in production networks.

sections.title: MPTCP Implementations and Deployments
sections.content: Multipath TCP was standardized as an experimental protocol in RFC 6824, and has since been implemented on Linux, macOS, iOS, FreeBSD, Oracle Solaris, and in Citrix load balancers. The most widespread deployment is Apple's implementation on iOS and macOS since iOS 7, which serves hundreds of millions of devices. The Siri voice assistant uses MPTCP to operate reliably even when moving between cellular and WiFi networks. Linux and FreeBSD implementations are open-source and widely deployed by researchers and operators. This RFC documents the operational lessons learned from these real deployments, collected from technical papers, mailing-list discussions, and packet traces from production systems.
sections.eli5: MPTCP is already running on your iPhone and Mac. This RFC explains what we learned from using it with real people.

sections.title: Where MPTCP Helps
sections.content:
Datacenters use load balancing to create multiple paths between servers. Even when both servers are single-homed, datacenter traffic can take different paths based on port or IP hash. MPTCP enables better utilization by splitting a connection across these load-balanced paths. Measurement studies show measurable throughput gains in production datacenters.

Mobile devices with WiFi and cellular interfaces are the largest MPTCP deployment. Three modes emerged: simultaneous use (using both networks at once for faster downloads), backup mode (using cellular only if WiFi fails), and single-path mode (staying on WiFi but quickly switching to cellular if WiFi dies). The backup and single-path modes help preserve battery life. Short connections benefit most from seamless handover between networks without dropping the connection.

Proxies allow MPTCP clients to reach regular TCP servers. HTTP proxies work for web traffic, while SOCKS proxies work for any application. Korea Telecom deployed a commercial MPTCP service through SOCKS proxies in 2015, achieving 850 Mbps throughput. Hybrid access networks combine wired and cellular access, using MPTCP at the edge to spread traffic across both.
sections.eli5: MPTCP works in server farms (using multiple wires at once), on phones (switching between WiFi and 4G smoothly), and through gateways (letting old servers work with MPTCP clients).

sections.title: Making It Work: Middleboxes and Networks
sections.content:
The biggest challenge is middlebox interference. Firewalls, NATs, and transparent proxies can break MPTCP by removing its options, changing sequence numbers, or modifying packet payloads. MPTCP was designed with fallback mechanisms: if a middlebox strips the MP_CAPABLE option from the initial SYN, MPTCP falls back to regular TCP automatically. Measurement data from the multipath-tcp.org server showed that among 184,000 MPTCP connections, only 125 had to fall back to TCP—a 99.93% success rate. HTTP transparent proxies occasionally caused fallbacks on the server-to-client direction, likely from proxies in cellular or enterprise networks. The tracebox tool, an extension of traceroute, helps network operators locate where middlebox interference occurs.

Congestion control must fairly share available bandwidth across subflows. The coupled congestion-control algorithm in RFC 6356 adapts NewReno to multiple paths. The OLIA algorithm provides better responsiveness on some paths. Delay-based algorithms exist but perform poorly when paths have very different characteristics. BALIA offers a better balance between fairness and responsiveness. Implementation chose OLIA as default on some systems.

Subflow management determines when and how many subflows to create. The full-mesh strategy creates one subflow per interface pair, useful for multihomed clients talking to single-homed servers. The ndiffport strategy creates multiple subflows between the same addresses, exploiting load-balancing diversity. A more flexible approach exposes kernel events to a user-space daemon, allowing policy-based subflow creation.
sections.eli5: The hard parts: making it work through firewalls (it usually does), sharing speed fairly across roads (different algorithms work differently), and deciding how many subflows to open (depends on the situation).

sections.title: Scheduling, Packet Size, and Performance Challenges
sections.content:
Packet scheduling picks which subflow transmits each segment. Round-robin sends equally. Lowest-RTT-first prioritizes faster paths. Studies show lowest-RTT-first performs best on average, but the optimal strategy depends on path characteristics. A pluggable architecture lets implementations experiment.

Maximum Segment Size (MSS) differences between subflows create surprising performance problems. If one subflow has MSS 1420 and another 1428, selecting MSS 1428 forces the 1420 subflow to split segments, wasting congestion window space. Selecting MSS 1420 underutilizes the faster subflow. Recent implementations adaptively select MSS based on each subflow's estimated contribution to total throughput, accounting for window utilization overhead.

DNS interactions cause issues on multihomed clients. A smartphone querying DNS over WiFi might get one CDN server address, while the same query over cellular gets a different one. When MPTCP then uses both paths, it may violate CDN-ISP contracts requiring access from within the ISP. One solution: use EDNS client subnet to advertise that the client can reach CDN servers via either interface.

When a slow subflow retransmits data already acknowledged on a faster subflow, TCP's retransmission logic keeps occupying the window. One operational solution: detect this state and send RST to reset the slow subflow, then immediately open a fresh one to send new data.
sections.eli5: Details matter: which road you send each packet on, how big the packets are (different roads, different sizes), what DNS tells you about where to go, and what happens when one road gets congested.

sections.title: Edge Cases in Production
sections.content:
Captive portals on open WiFi networks interfere with MPTCP. A smartphone prefers WiFi over cellular, so it tries to create the initial subflow over WiFi. If WiFi has a captive portal blocking internet access, the connection hangs waiting for WiFi to work. A better strategy: try WiFi for a few attempts, then also try cellular for the initial subflow to ensure connectivity.

Stateless web servers use SYN cookies for DDoS protection. MPTCP negotiates keys in the three-way handshake and echoes them in the third ACK. If the third ACK is lost (happens under packet loss), the server cannot reconstruct MPTCP state. Unlike regular TCP data segments (which are retransmitted), the third ACK is not reliably delivered, so MPTCP falls back to TCP unnecessarily in lossy environments. Proposed solutions add a reliable handshake mechanism after the three-way handshake.

Load-balanced server farms deploy thousands of servers behind a virtual IP (VIP) with Layer 4 load balancers that route flows to specific servers. MPTCP creates multiple subflows with different port numbers; all subflows of one connection must route to the same server. Load balancers must track the MPTCP token in MP_JOIN options. When multiple load balancers exist for redundancy, they would need to synchronize MPTCP state—impractical at scale. Proposed solutions modify the MP_CAPABLE handshake to let servers encode routing information into the token.
sections.eli5: Real networks have quirks: WiFi login walls, servers protecting against hacking, and huge farms of load-balanced machines. MPTCP must handle all of them.

sections.title: Security and Deployment Notes
sections.content: MPTCP sends packets from one connection over different paths. This breaks assumptions held by middleboxes like firewalls and intrusion detection systems (IDS), which expect to see all packets of a connection. A smartphone in an enterprise network connected to a corporate network via VPN might send packets over both the enterprise and cellular paths; the enterprise firewall sees only some of the traffic. Similarly, deep packet inspection (DPI) systems cannot see all packets. RFC 7430 provides a comprehensive analysis of remaining MPTCP security issues. The RFC recommends strong authentication of provisioning-domain information and careful design of source address selection to prevent attacks where an attacker on one path influences traffic on another path.
sections.eli5: Firewalls that spy on all traffic see only half the connection now. Security needs thought when connections can travel multiple paths.
